set.n: Old half-dollars washed out of the Wisconsin River bank, Portage (1887)
set.pl: Left bank of the Wisconsin River 'above the point' at Portage, where the bank had washed away (Portage paper, 1887); 'the point' is not yet identified, so the ring covers the river front at Portage.
set.st: On 9 Apr 1887 a raftsman found a silver piece where the river bank above 'the point' at Portage had worn away. Digging turned up old fifty-cent pieces (one dated 1828), $57 at first and over $100 in all; men and boys dug all day until the rising river covered the spot. It was supposed some early traveller buried it there for safe keeping. Pin is approximate, not the spot itself.
set.t: Partly recovered; the rest may have washed downstream. Riverbank: check public access and DNR rules.
pinev: Portage paper, 16 Apr 1887: left bank above 'the point' at Portage; the point is not yet identified, so r2000 covers the Portage river front.
set.tovw: Lead grade D (treasure thread): a recovered spill, digging stopped by the rising river, strays possible
